target.title: fix(memory-wiki): disambiguate the reserved index page stem for synthesis and ingest
target.body:
## Summary

A memory-wiki `create_synthesis` or source `ingest` whose title slugifies to `index` silently loses the stored fact. The page is written to `<dir>/index.md`, which is the auto-generated directory-index file: it is excluded from all page scanning (so `wiki_search` / `wiki_get` / digest never see it) and is destructively overwritten by the generated directory-index block on the next compile, which the same call triggers. The result is that the content is both unretrievable and clobbered on disk. "Index" is a natural title for an overview page, so this is reachable in normal usage.

## Root cause

The collision happens only at the **direct page-stem boundary**. `applyCreateSynthesisMutation` (`apply.ts:226`) and `ingestMemoryWikiSource` (`ingest.ts:48`) build a bare `<dir>/<slug>.md` path straight from `slugifyWikiSegment(title)`:

```ts
// apply.ts (before)
const slug = slugifyWikiSegment(params.mutation.title);
const pagePath = path.join("syntheses", `${slug}.md`).replace(/\\/g, "/");
```

For title "Index" that resolves to `syntheses/index.md`. `index.md` is the only compiler-owned page filename in these directories: `compile.ts:1413` writes `<dir>/index.md` per page group, and `compile.ts:368`, `query.ts:251`, `status.ts:94` all exclude `index.md` from page scanning.

## Fix

Add a dedicated `slugifyWikiPageStem` helper that escapes the reserved `index` stem, and route only the two direct page writers through it. `slugifyWikiSegment` itself is left unchanged:

```ts
// markdown.ts (after)
const WIKI_RESERVED_PAGE_STEMS = new Set(["index"]);

export function slugifyWikiPageStem(raw: string): string {
  const slug = slugifyWikiSegment(raw);
  if (!WIKI_RESERVED_PAGE_STEMS.has(slug)) {
    return slug;
  }
  const suffix = createHash("sha1").update(raw).digest("hex").slice(0, WIKI_SEGMENT_HASH_BYTES);
  return `${slug}-${suffix}`;
}
```

`apply.ts` and `ingest.ts` now call `slugifyWikiPageStem(title)`. A title of "Index" slugifies to `index-<hash>`, a normal scannable page, while the generated `<dir>/index.md` stays owned by the compiler.

## Scope: only `index` is reserved

The escape covers exactly the stem that is compiler-owned in the synthesis/ingest page directories. `log` is deliberately not reserved: the compiler never writes `<dir>/log.md` (the only generated page file per group is `index.md`), and nothing excludes `log.md` from page scanning. The memory-wiki run log lives at `.openclaw-wiki/log.jsonl`, and `OKF_RESERVED_FILENAMES`'s `log.md` is specific to the OKF import format, not these page directories. So a title "Log" resolves to a normal, retrievable `syntheses/log.md` / `sources/log.md` and keeps its existing direct path with no churn.

## Why this is the right boundary

The reserved escape belongs at the direct page-stem allocation, not in the shared slug helper. `slugifyWikiSegment` is also consumed by `bridge`, `unsafe-local`, and `okf`, which compose its output into prefixed and hashed persisted identities that can never equal a bare `index.md`:

- `bridge.ts:113-115`: `workspaceSlug = ${slugifyWikiSegment(name)}-${hash}`, final file `bridge-<workspaceSlug>-<artifactSlug>`.
- `unsafe-local.ts:110-115`: `pageSlug = ${baseSlug}-${hash}-${baseSlug}-${hash}`, final file `unsafe-local-<pageSlug>`.
- `okf.ts:117/124/128`: composed into `okf-<bundleKey>-<slug>-<hash>`, and OKF additionally guards its own write path via `OKF_RESERVED_FILENAMES`.

Putting the escape inside `slugifyWikiSegment` would have changed those persisted page ids/paths whenever a component was named `index`, leaving stale duplicate pages and shifting lookups on upgrade. Scoping it to `slugifyWikiPageStem` keeps `slugifyWikiSegment` output byte-stable (verified identical to `main`), so the composed callers are untouched and no migration is needed. The change is additive and deterministic (SHA1 of the raw title). Distinct from open PR #93843 (distinct titles colliding to the same slug); that PR's `resolveTitleKeyedWikiSlug` still computes `slugifyWikiSegment(title)` as its base, so the two compose. Possible rebase overlap with #93843 in `markdown.ts` only.

## Verification

From a deps-enabled checkout, rebased onto current `origin/main`:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs reserved-index-collision.repro.test.ts markdown.test.ts apply.test.ts ingest.test.ts okf.test.ts` - 26 passed. The sibling suites confirm composed identities are unchanged.
- New repro: 2 retrieval cases fail on pristine main, pass with patch; the contract case asserts `slugifyWikiSegment("Index") === "index"` (shared output stable), `slugifyWikiPageStem("Index")` matches `/^index-[0-9a-f]{12}$/`, and `slugifyWikiPageStem("Log") === "log"` (not reserved, no churn).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <changed files>` - clean
- `oxfmt --check <changed files>` - all 4 files correctly formatted
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` - both clean

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a memory-wiki synthesis or source ingest titled "Index" is silently lost (written to the compiler-owned `<dir>/index.md`, unreachable by search/get); after the fix it lands at a disambiguated `index-<hash>` page and stays retrievable.
Real environment tested: drove the real `applyMemoryWikiMutation`, `ingestMemoryWikiSource`, `searchMemoryWiki`, and `getMemoryWikiPage` against an on-disk vault built by the real `createMemoryWikiTestHarness` (no stubs of the wiki runtime), on pristine `main@9ff7abc8989c1770856b27d5b06e6bb6695ce666` and on PR head `dc5f1cd0a5b032b9977606a31bc5d5b20a163bfb`, with identical inputs.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: drove `applyMemoryWikiMutation({op:"create_synthesis", title:"Index", body:"Durable synthesis body that must survive."})` then `ingestMemoryWikiSource({title:"Index"})`, and queried each back with `searchMemoryWiki` / `getMemoryWikiPage`, capturing the observed page path and retrievability.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 9ff7abc8989c1770856b27d5b06e6bb6695ce666)
create_synthesis title="Index" -> pagePath=syntheses/index.md
wiki_search(synthesis) retrievable=false
wiki_get(synthesis) body_present=false
on_disk(synthesis) body_present=true
ingest title="Index" -> pagePath=sources/index.md
wiki_search(ingest) retrievable=false

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head dc5f1cd0a5b032b9977606a31bc5d5b20a163bfb)
create_synthesis title="Index" -> pagePath=syntheses/index-c2df9b932637.md
wiki_search(synthesis) retrievable=true
wiki_get(synthesis) body_present=true
on_disk(synthesis) body_present=true
ingest title="Index" -> pagePath=sources/index-c2df9b932637.md
wiki_search(ingest) retrievable=true
```
Observed result after fix: on pristine main the "Index" synthesis and ingest write to `<dir>/index.md` and are unretrievable (`retrievable=false`, `body_present=false`) even though bytes sit on disk; with the patch both move to the disambiguated `index-c2df9b932637.md` page and become fully retrievable by both `searchMemoryWiki` and `getMemoryWikiPage`.
What was not tested: a full build and broad cross-suite run were not exercised on this OOM-constrained box; the scope is one new slug helper plus the two direct page writers, and the byte-stability of the shared `slugifyWikiSegment` output for bridge/unsafe-local/OKF identities is asserted by the colocated regression suite rather than re-driven here.

target.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly
target.body:
## Summary

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix for embedded-agent provider routing and model alias owner selection.
- Root cause: The resolver made the `azure-openai-responses` canonicalization decision from alias-level API adapter and model-row presence alone, instead of separating Azure endpoint ownership surface from manifest-suppressed models. That caused codex-only models to be owned by Azure in one path, provider-level Azure custom deployment names to be canonicalized back to OpenAI in another path, and manifest-only Azure alias rows to keep Azure ownership even when no Azure endpoint was configured.
- Intended outcome: Keep `azure-openai-responses` ownership when the requested model has actual Azure Responses endpoint surface through config or alias metadata, but canonicalize manifest-suppressed alias models and endpoint-less aliases back to the target OpenAI owner.
- Current update: Rebased onto current `main`, resolved the static-catalog conflict by preserving both the bundled-plugin config filter and model-catalog suppression logic, then re-ran focused resolver tests, lint, test typecheck, and diff whitespace validation on the updated head.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High for the resolver boundary. The remaining decision is whether the mock Azure Responses probe is sufficient proof for this auth-provider routing bug or whether maintainers require a live Azure account credential exchange.

What problem does this PR solve?

`azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5` embedded-agent/probe routes were being treated like a pure OpenAI provider alias, so the request could resolve through OpenAI provider/auth metadata instead of the configured Azure Responses provider. The first fix preserved every transport-overriding alias on the requested provider, but CI showed that was too broad: `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` then reported the codex-only OAuth error as an Azure Responses model instead of the OpenAI-owned model.

Why does this matter now?

The linked issue is an auth/provider-selection bug: Azure Responses routes need to keep Azure provider identity for real Azure deployments, while OpenAI codex-only models still need OpenAI-owned OAuth guidance. Mixing those owners gives users the wrong remediation path and can mask the actual credential boundary.

What is the intended outcome?

The resolver keeps `azure-openai-responses` when the requested model has actual Azure Responses endpoint surface: a configured Azure base URL, a matching configured model row with endpoint surface, or alias metadata that declares an endpoint. If the alias/model is explicitly manifest-suppressed, such as the codex-only model, or the manifest alias only names an API adapter without an Azure endpoint, the alias can canonicalize back to its OpenAI owner so the error or fallback does not mix Azure ownership with the OpenAI API endpoint.

What is intentionally out of scope?

This PR does not change the OpenAI plugin manifest, provider runtime implementations, auth profile storage, public config shape, migrations, schema, or Azure API behavior. It only tightens embedded-agent model alias owner selection.

What does success look like?

- `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5` with Azure Responses config resolves as provider `azure-openai-responses`, api `azure-openai-responses`, and the configured Azure base URL.
- `azure-openai-responses/customer-gpt-deployment` with provider-level Azure transport config resolves under the Azure provider owner instead of `openai/customer-gpt-deployment`.
- `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` with no Azure model row reports the OpenAI codex-only owner: `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, including when provider-level Azure transport config exists.
- `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5` without configured or declared Azure endpoint surface canonicalizes back to the OpenAI owner instead of producing an Azure-owned model pointed at the OpenAI API endpoint.
- Pure provider aliases such as `moonshot-ai -> moonshot` continue to canonicalize normally.

What should reviewers focus on?

Please focus on whether the owner boundary is correct: transport aliases are preserved only for models that actually have alias/config catalog surface, while missing alias models fall back to the target provider owner for errors and guidance.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #93781

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related CI failure: `checks-node-agentic-agents-embedded` on the previous PR head failed because `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` produced an Azure-owned error string instead of the expected OpenAI codex-only OAuth hint.

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No direct maintainer request on the PR. The linked issue and failing CI identify the provider/auth routing regression.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5` model/probe routing keeps the Azure Responses provider, API, base URL, and auth route instead of falling back to OpenAI; this update also restores the OpenAI owner for missing codex-only Azure alias requests.
- Real environment tested: Prior real OpenClaw `models status --probe` proof used a local mock Responses server on Darwin 25.5.0 arm64, Node v24.15.0, OpenClaw v2026.6.8. Current CI repair validation ran on Linux with Node/pnpm in the PR worktree.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  # Prior real routing/probe proof with a temporary OpenClaw config containing:
  # models.providers.azure-openai-responses.api=azure-openai-responses
  # models.providers.azure-openai-responses.baseUrl=<mock Responses server>/openai/v1
  # models.providers.azure-openai-responses.models[0].id=gpt-5.5
  OPENCLAW_HOME=<temp-home> \
    OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<temp-openclaw.json> \
    OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<temp-state> \
    pnpm openclaw models status --json --probe \
      --probe-provider azure-openai-responses \
      --probe-timeout 10000 \
      --probe-max-tokens 1

  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.forward-compat.errors-and-overrides.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.static-catalog.test.ts

  pnpm lint --threads=8
  pnpm check:test-types
  git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
  ```
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):
  ```json
  {
    "command": "pnpm openclaw models status --json --probe --probe-provider azure-openai-responses --probe-timeout 10000 --probe-max-tokens 1",
    "exitCode": 0,
    "resolvedDefault": "azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5",
    "defaultModel": "azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5",
    "missingProvidersInUse": [],
    "probe": {
      "totalTargets": 1,
      "results": [
        {
          "provider": "azure-openai-responses",
          "model": "azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5",
          "source": "models.json",
          "status": "ok"
        }
      ]
    },
    "mockRequests": [
      {
        "method": "POST",
        "url": "/openai/v1/responses?api-version=preview",
        "authorizationPresent": false,
        "apiKeyHeaderPresent": true,
        "bodyModel": "gpt-5.5",
        "stream": true,
        "maxOutputTokens": 1
      }
    ]
  }
  ```
  ```text
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.forward-compat.errors-and-overrides.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.static-catalog.test.ts
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
  Tests  170 passed (170)
  [test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 73.08s

  pnpm lint --threads=8
  $ node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8
  [oxlint:core] finished
  [oxlint:extensions] finished
  [oxlint:scripts] finished

  pnpm check:test-types
  $ pnpm tsgo:test
  $ pnpm tsgo:core:test && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test

  git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
  Validation result: pass, exit_code=0, 133ms
  ```
- Observed result after fix: The real OpenClaw probe path created one Azure Responses probe target, reported `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5`, and sent the request to the configured Azure Responses base URL with an API-key header. The current regression validation also shows provider-level Azure custom deployment names stay on `azure-openai-responses`, provider-level codex-only requests still report `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark`, and configured Azure Responses routes stay on Azure for both explicit model rows and provider-level Azure transport config without `models[]`.
- What was not tested: Live Azure account credentials.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The routing/probe proof uses a local mock Responses server to validate OpenClaw provider routing without external credentials. The current Linux environment could validate the CI-failing resolver behavior and typecheck, but did not have live Azure credentials for a real Azure account probe.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): The previous PR head failed `checks-node-agentic-agents-embedded` because the codex-only test expected `Unknown model: openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark...` but received `Unknown model: azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.3-codex-spark...`.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.forward-compat.errors-and-overrides.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.static-catalog.test.ts

pnpm lint --threads=8
pnpm check:test-types
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- Added coverage for `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.3-codex-spark` when the Azure provider is configured but does not declare that model row; the error must come from `openai/gpt-5.3-codex-spark`.
- Added coverage for provider-level Azure Responses config without `models[]`; a discovered OpenAI catalog model still resolves under the requested `azure-openai-responses` owner when Azure transport overrides are configured.
- Added coverage for provider-level Azure custom deployment names, which must keep the Azure provider owner even when the deployment name is not in the bundled OpenAI catalog.
- Added coverage that provider-level Azure codex-only aliases remain OpenAI-owned through manifest suppression instead of being treated like custom Azure deployments.
- Added coverage that endpoint-less manifest Azure aliases canonicalize back to OpenAI instead of keeping Azure ownership while inheriting the OpenAI API endpoint.
- Kept the existing Azure Responses route coverage for `azure-openai-responses/gpt-5.5`, which must stay on the Azure provider, Azure API adapter, and configured Azure base URL.
- Existing pure provider alias coverage still protects non-transport aliases such as `moonshot-ai -> moonshot`.

What failed before this fix, if known?

The CI shard `checks-node-agentic-agents-embedded` failed on the prior PR head because the broad transport-override preservation kept the codex-only OpenAI model under `azure-openai-responses` for the unknown-model error owner.

If no test was added, why not?

A test was added for the configured-Azure/no-matching-model-row case, and the existing CI-failing codex-only test now passes.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes. Error ownership for missing Azure alias models now falls back to the target provider when the Azure alias has no matching model surface, while real Azure alias model routes keep Azure provider identity.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

No. Existing config fields are interpreted more precisely; no new config, environment variable, schema, migration, or default value is introduced.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`)

Yes, in the narrow provider/auth routing sense: model owner selection now keeps Azure auth routing only for actual Azure alias models and keeps OpenAI OAuth guidance for OpenAI-owned codex-only models.

What is the highest-risk area?

Provider owner selection for transport-overriding manifest aliases.

How is that risk mitigated?

The fix uses configured Azure endpoint surface as the source of truth for Azure ownership, model rows as model-specific routing evidence, and manifest suppression as the explicit blocklist for models that must remain target-provider owned. Related tests cover the boundary: configured Azure `gpt-5.5` and custom deployments stay Azure, endpoint-less Azure manifest aliases canonicalize back to OpenAI, and codex-only `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` reports through OpenAI even with provider-level Azure transport config.

## Current review state

What is the next action?

Ready for CI to re-run on the rebased head, then maintainer review of the auth-provider owner boundary and proof level.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?

- CI needs to re-run on the updated head.
- Live Azure account testing was not performed; the supplied real behavior proof uses a local mock Responses server to validate OpenClaw routing/probe behavior without external credentials.
- The remaining maintainer decision is whether mock Azure Responses routing proof is sufficient for this resolver-layer auth-provider bug.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?

- RF-001: The resolver boundary is explicitly stated above: configured Azure endpoint/model surface keeps Azure ownership; manifest-suppressed or endpoint-less aliases fall back to the OpenAI owner. This remains a maintainer acceptance point because it changes auth-provider owner selection.
- RF-002: Live Azure credential proof is not available in this environment; the PR body discloses that limitation and keeps the mock Responses server proof scoped to OpenClaw routing/probe behavior.
- RF-003: Re-ran `pnpm lint --threads=8` on the rebased head; passed.
- RF-004: Re-ran the focused embedded-agent model vitest command on the rebased head; 3 files and 170 tests passed.
- RF-005: Re-ran `pnpm check:test-types` on the rebased head; passed.
- RF-006: The previously observed CI success was for the old PR head, so it is treated as advisory only; this update relies on fresh local validation and waits for CI on the new head.

target.title: fix: diagnose Windows LAN Gateway firewall blocks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who bind the Gateway to LAN on Windows can see a healthy loopback probe and an advertised Control UI LAN URL even when Windows Firewall blocks other devices from reaching that URL.

Related context: materialized OpenClaw claim `ACTIONABLE-002-C3-inconclusive-windows-firewall-gateway-port`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a read-only Windows Firewall diagnostic for local LAN Gateway status and setup/configure output. The diagnostic inspects active Windows network profiles and matching inbound rules without mutating firewall policy, then surfaces actionable warnings for missing allow rules, local-rule policy, profile mismatch, scoped rules, and bounded inspection failures.

## User Impact

Windows users get a concrete firewall warning when OpenClaw advertises a LAN Control UI URL that loopback can reach but LAN clients may not. Users are guided to add an appropriate inbound TCP allow rule or use loopback, Tailscale, or SSH tunneling instead of LAN binding.

target.title: Idr msteams adaptive card tables
target.body: ## Summary **What problem does this PR solve?** Microsoft Teams renders markdown tables as plain-text code blocks (```` ``` ````-wrapped ASCII tables), which are hard to read on mobile, lose column alignment in narrow viewports, and cannot be scrolled horizontally. Teams natively supports Adaptive Card Table/TableRow/TableCell elements (schema 1.5+) that render as proper visual tables with headers, grid lines, and responsive cell wrapping. **Why does this matter now?** Enterprise deployments using OpenClaw via Teams frequently produce tabular data (comparison tables, status reports, structured outputs). Users report that code-block tables are the single biggest readability issue on Teams mobile and narrow desktop panes. **What is the intended outcome?** - Markdown tables in agent replies are automatically rendered as native Adaptive Card Table elements in Teams - Text before/after tables is delivered as regular markdown messages - The feature is the default for msteams but opt-out via config (`channels.msteams.markdown.tables: "code"`) - Other channels are unaffected **What is intentionally out of scope?** - Adaptive Card rendering for non-table content (lists, headings, etc.) - Nested tables or tables with merged cells - The EKG identity JWT signing (organization-specific, handled separately) - Streaming/draft table rendering (tables only render in final reply) **What does success look like?** Agent replies containing markdown tables appear as formatted, scrollable, grid-aligned tables in Teams desktop, web, and mobile clients. **What should reviewers focus on?** - The `splitTextAndTables` placeholder offset logic — off-by-one errors would corrupt message ordering - The `buildActivity` early return for `adaptiveCard` messages — ensure it doesn't skip AI-generated entity marking - Whether `"adaptive"` mode in `convertMarkdownTables` (pass-through) has unintended effects on other code paths that call it ## Linked context **Which issue does this close?** Closes # _(first-time contribution — no existing issue yet; will file one if maintainers prefer)_ **Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?** - The existing `"block"` table mode infrastructure (added but runtime-degraded to `"code"`) was designed for this use case - Adaptive Card schema 1.5 Table element spec: https://adaptivecards.io/explorer/Table.html **Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?** No — this is an external contributor PR addressing a pain point encountered in production Teams deployments. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - **Behavior or issue addressed:** Markdown tables in agent replies render as unreadable code blocks in Teams; now render as native Adaptive Card tables - **Real environment tested:** Docker deployment (ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:2026.5.12) with msteams channel connected to Azure Bot Service, tested on Teams desktop (Windows) and Teams mobile (iOS) - **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Sent a prompt that produces a comparison table (e.g. "Compare Python vs JavaScript in a table"), observed the reply in Teams - **Evidence after fix:** Agent reply splits into text message + Adaptive Card with grid-rendered table headers/rows. Table is scrollable and wraps on mobile. - **Observed result after fix:** Tables render with bold headers, visible grid lines, proper cell text wrapping. Non-table text around the table is delivered as separate plain messages. - **What was not tested:** Tables with 10+ columns (may overflow Adaptive Card width limits on narrow screens), deeply nested markdown inside table cells (only plain text supported) - **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Cannot share screenshots as they contain internal enterprise data. Can reproduce on request with sanitized test prompts. - **Before evidence:** Tables previously appeared as monospace code blocks, often with broken alignment on mobile due to character width variance. Example Screen shot : Before : Markdown After: Adaptive Card ## Tests and validation **Which commands did you run?** ``` pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/adaptive-card-table.test.ts pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/messenger.test.ts ``` **What regression coverage was added or updated?** - `adaptive-card-table.test.ts` — unit tests for `buildAdaptiveCardTable` (card structure, empty cells) and `splitTextAndTables` (no tables, single table, table at start/end, multiple tables) - `messenger.test.ts` — integration tests for `renderReplyPayloadsToMessages` with `tableMode: "adaptive"` (tables render as cards, no-table passthrough) and `buildActivity` adaptive card attachment handling **What failed before this fix, if known?** No failure — this is additive behavior. The previous `"code"` mode still works as fallback. **If no test was added, why not?** Tests were added. ## Risk checklist **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — msteams table rendering changes from code blocks to Adaptive Cards (default). Users can revert via config. **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new `"adaptive"` value in `MarkdownTableMode` enum; new default for msteams channel. Existing `channels.msteams.markdown.tables: "code"` configs continue working. **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** No. **What is the highest-risk area?** The `renderAdaptiveTablePayload` function parsing tables from raw markdown at send time — if the markdown-it parser or IR layer has edge cases with malformed tables, it could produce empty/broken cards. **How is that risk mitigated?** - Falls back to text-only rendering when `markdownToIRWithMeta` returns zero tables - The `splitTextAndTables` function handles all edge cases (empty text, table at boundaries) - Users can opt out immediately via `channels.msteams.markdown.tables: "code"` ## Current review state **What is the next action?** Ready for maintainer review. Author can provide live proof screenshots with sanitized test data on request. **What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?** Waiting on maintainer review. CI will run on push. **Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?** N/A — first submission.

target.title: fix(browser): notify agent when click triggers download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a browser `/act` action triggers a file download, OpenClaw already saves the unmanaged Playwright download, but the agent-visible `/act` response did not include the downloaded filename or saved path.

That meant an agent could successfully trigger a download, receive only a generic success response, and then retry because it had no completion/path feedback for the saved file.

Fixes #93250

## Why This Change Was Made

This change adds action-scoped download capture around Playwright-backed `/act` execution and returns optional `downloads` metadata in the `/act` JSON response.

The response includes the saved path and suggested filename for downloads observed during click, coordinate click, batch, and evaluate actions. The `downloads` payload is page-level observation metadata for the action window, not an exclusive ownership claim: overlapping `/act` calls on the same page may receive the same saved download so the browser event is not silently dropped.

## User Impact

Agents can now see that a browser-triggered download completed, including where the file was saved, and avoid retrying an action that already produced the expected file.

Existing `/act` responses remain compatible: the `downloads` field is optional and only appears when a download is captured.

## Evidence

Live click-triggered `/act` proof on macOS, Node.js v26.0.0, Chrome 149.0.7827.197:

```bash
$ curl --noproxy '*' -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:53558/
HTTP 200
```

target.title: fix(gateway): exit 0 on EADDRINUSE when healthy OpenClaw gateway is already running
target.body:
## Problem
When `openclaw gateway run` hits EADDRINUSE, it exits with code 1. Under systemd/launchd with `Restart=on-failure`, this creates a tight crash-loop.

## Root Cause
`GatewayLockError` on port conflict always exited non-zero, even when an already-healthy OpenClaw gateway was listening on that port.

## Fix
On EADDRINUSE, probe the gateway using the correct bind/TLS-aware URL with resolved auth credentials. Exit 0 only when a healthy OpenClaw instance is confirmed. Exit 1 for foreign processes or failed probes.

Probe handles all auth modes:
- **shared-secret** (token/password): forwarded directly
- **trusted-proxy**: synthetic proxy headers derived from config instead of shared-secret credentials
- **TLS with self-signed cert**: fingerprint loaded from `loadGatewayTlsRuntime` and pinned for the probe

Also fixes a pre-existing type error in `src/cli/update-cli.test.ts`.

Supersedes #29499 — thanks @BlueBirdBack for identifying the issue.

---

- [x] Built with Claude (Kees/OpenClaw) + Codex
- [x] Fully tested: VM gates (pnpm build + check + vitest gateway-cli + probe)
- [x] Author understands what the code does

target.title: fix(agents): preserve streamed assistant text when Claude CLI result event is empty
target.body:
## Summary

- The claude `stream-json` dialect can emit a final `result` event with **empty text** even though assistant text deltas were already streamed (or the turn was tool-only). Both JSONL parsers trust the final event and discard everything accumulated, so the CLI runner throws `CLI backend returned an empty response.` (`reason=empty_response`) and the gateway falls back to the next model — **losing a reply that had already fully arrived**.
- Fix (parser-only): when the `result` event has no text, fall back to the accumulated streamed deltas instead of dropping them, in **both** `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` and `parseCliJsonl`. A structured `CliOutput.hadToolCalls` flag (set via `claudeRecordHasToolUseBlock` / the existing `isClaudeToolUseBlockType`) is also recorded so a verifiably tool-only turn can be told apart from a genuinely empty reply.
- **The runner's empty-response failover contract is unchanged.** An earlier revision of this PR added a `hadToolCalls`-based bypass in `cli-runner.ts`; that was removed (commit `ac2f807c`, following Option 1 of the review). Today an empty turn — tool-only or not — still fails over by default, and only stays silent when the caller already set `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent`. **This PR no longer touches `cli-runner.ts`** (it is byte-identical to `main`); the only behavioral change lives in the two parsers.
- The parser already half-acknowledges this case — `parseClaudeCliJsonlResult` deliberately keeps session metadata when the result text is empty (*"Keep the resolved session handle and usage instead of dropping them"*). This PR extends the same reasoning to the streamed assistant text itself.
- Safety: if the model genuinely returned nothing, the accumulated text is also empty, so the `FailoverError` fires exactly as before. Non-Claude dialects are untouched (`hadToolCalls` stays `undefined`).
- Reviewers should focus on: the fallback expression in **both** parsers and the structured tool_use detection helper (`claudeRecordHasToolUseBlock`). `cli-runner.ts` is **not** part of this diff.
- The vulnerable path (`if (result) { output = result; return; }`) is still present on `main` and in the published `2026.6.8` tarball (`dist/claude-live-session-*.js` / `dist/cli-output-*.js`); see the 2026-06-16 comment confirming it is not fixed natively in 6.7/6.8.

## Tests

- `cli-output.test.ts`: 4 new cases — streamed text preserved on empty result (both parsers), tool-only flag set (both parsers); updated the existing "preserves Claude session metadata even when the final result text is empty" expectation (`hadToolCalls: false`).
- `cli-runner.reliability.test.ts`: focused coverage that a verifiably tool-only empty turn (tool_use block + empty result) **fails over by default** (`empty_response`) and only returns the silent payload when `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` is set — i.e. the prior fallback contract is preserved.
- `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` run locally (macOS): the only failures are environment-specific (host locale leaking into `Intl` formatting asserts and `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` symlink canonicalization), none in the touched files.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Claude CLI turns streamed a full reply, but the final `result` event arrived with empty text; the gateway threw `CLI backend returned an empty response.` (`reason=empty_response`) and fell back to `openai/gpt-5.5`, discarding the streamed reply. Tool-only turns hit the same false failover.
- Real environment tested: production OpenClaw **2026.6.1** gateway on an Ubuntu VPS (systemd service), `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-haiku-4-5` via the claude-cli backend, fallback chain to `openai/gpt-5.5`, live Discord/WhatsApp channels and cron agents. Still reproducing through **2026.6.8** (see the 2026-06-16 comment).
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: applied the equivalent fix as a dist-bundle patch (same logic as this PR's source change) to `dist/claude-live-session-*.js` and `dist/cli-output-*.js`, validated with `node --check`, then `systemctl restart openclaw-gateway` (2026-06-04 13:56 BRT) and watched `journalctl -u openclaw-gateway -f` under normal production traffic; later verified with `ssh` to the host and `journalctl -u openclaw-gateway --since "14:26" | grep -c empty_response`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): redacted runtime logs / copied live output below. After the restart: `journalctl -u openclaw-gateway --since "14:26" | grep -c empty_response` → `0` (vs 3 occurrences earlier that same day), and the gateway boot shows claude sessions healthy:


target.title: fix #95351: [Feature]: Generic JSONL line-parsing hook for CliBackendPlugin (native tool-card support beyond claude-stream-json)

## Summary

- Problem: `CliBackendPlugin` backends that use `output: "jsonl"` had no public, backend-owned parser hook for provider-specific JSONL streams, so third-party CLIs with native tool execution could not feed OpenClaw's tool-card event path unless they impersonated a built-in dialect.
- Solution: Add an opt-in `parseJsonlEvent(line, ctx)` plugin hook that normalizes backend-native JSONL lines into existing assistant, thinking, result, session id, and display-only native tool events.
- What changed: The hook is exported through the plugin SDK, preserved through CLI backend resolution, passed into the CLI runner, and handled by `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` before built-in Claude/Gemini JSONL parsing. Plugin hook tool events use display-only tool-card callbacks so they do not mutate messaging delivery evidence.
- Follow-up update: Synced the branch onto current `origin/main` again as main moved, resolving `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` by regenerating the derived baseline and reconciling `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` with the current public SDK surface budget (`exports: 10413`, `callable exports: 5223`, `deprecated exports: 3257`). Current-head CI follow-up also regenerated `docs/docs_map.md` after `check-docs` found it stale. Earlier updates also removed the lint-only unnecessary test assertion flagged by ClawSweeper/CI.
- What did NOT change: This does not change the `agents.defaults.cliBackends.*.jsonlDialect` config schema, does not add a new built-in dialect value, does not execute plugin-reported tools through OpenClaw's tool catalog, does not let plugin display events count as message delivery evidence, and does not change Claude/Gemini stream-json semantics.
- Fixes #95351

## What Problem This Solves

Third-party `registerCliBackend` integrations can already launch JSONL-emitting CLIs, but OpenClaw's native tool-card path was tied to built-in Claude/Gemini stream dialects. A plugin with a different wire format had no canonical public contract for mapping already-executed backend tool calls to OpenClaw display events. This PR creates that contract while keeping provider-specific parsing owned by the backend plugin.

## Evidence

Local verification covered the parser behavior, backend resolution path, public SDK export surface, API baseline update, display-only runner isolation, lint cleanliness, strict build smoke, main-sync CI drift, and a local Control UI browser proof. The focused parser regression drives a Cursor-like JSONL sequence through `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` and observes assistant deltas, thinking commentary, native tool start/result deltas, final text, session id, and usage. The runner regression drives a plugin JSONL `message` tool card through `executePreparedCliRun` and verifies it renders tool events without setting messaging delivery evidence.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A plugin-owned CLI backend with `output: "jsonl"` can now translate provider-specific JSONL lines into OpenClaw display events, including native tool start/result cards, without selecting a built-in Claude or Gemini dialect.

The public contract surface is intentionally minimal and canonical: plugin code owns provider-specific wire parsing, OpenClaw owns normalized display events. Compatibility/default behavior is preserved because built-in `jsonlDialect` values and existing config schema remain unchanged. target.title: fix(cli): bound approvals file read size in exec-approvals-cli
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `--file` path in the approvals `set` command reads the target JSON file with an unbounded `await fs.readFile()`, so a user that accidentally passes a very large file (e.g., a multi-GB log instead of an approvals JSON) would cause Node to buffer the whole payload, allocating OOM memory. The `--stdin` path already has a 1 MB bound via `readStdin()` (`EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`), but the `--file` path was missing the equivalent guard.

This is a defense-in-depth fix and a sibling-consistency cleanup: in practice approvals JSON files are small (`{ version, agents: { ... } }`), but the file read should be bounded the way the already-merged stdin path is.

## Changes

- Add `readFileWithBound(filePath, maxBytes)` in `exec-approvals-cli.ts`, matching the pattern of the existing `readStdin()`. Uses `await fs.stat()` to check file size before `readFile()`, with the same 1 MB default cap (`EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`).
- Replace the `--file` read on the approvals `set` action handler with `readFileWithBound()`.
- Export `readFileWithBound` via the existing `testing` object for focused unit testing.
- Add a focused regression test in `exec-approvals-cli.test.ts` using a temp file at the boundary size to verify the cap, mirroring the existing `bounds approvals JSON read from stdin` test.
- Preserve all existing behavior: small valid files continue to parse through the same `JSON5.parse` and `saveSnapshotTargeted` path.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: An oversized `--file` approvals JSON must be rejected before read with an `Exec approvals file exceeds ... bytes` error. A normal-sized (valid) approvals file must continue to parse as before.
- **Real environment tested**: Local Vitest run on Node v22.22.0, exercising the real `fs.stat` + `fs.readFile` against a real temp file on an ext4 filesystem.
- **Exact steps**: `pnpm test src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts` — 13 tests pass including the new oversized-file regression for both the happy (small file within bound) and unhappy (file 1 byte over bound) paths.
- **Observed result**: All 13 tests pass. The new test creates a temp directory with a small file (resolves to expected content) and a large file (rejects with `Exec approvals file exceeds 100 bytes`). The existing 12 tests pass unmodified.
- **What was not tested**: The full `openclaw approvals set --file path` end-to-end command integration; the unit-level `readFileWithBound` helper owns the file read bound and is the correct coverage boundary, matching how `readStdin` is tested.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest:

```
$ pnpm test src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

Format (oxfmt):

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts
  (clean)
```

**Label**: security

_AI-assisted._

target.title: fix(scripts): retry Docker E2E after rejected resource caps
target.body:
Fixes #98601

## What Problem This Solves

Docker E2E and package-backed Docker lanes can fail before the test container starts when the local Docker daemon accepts the command but rejects OpenClaw's default `--memory`, `--cpus`, or `--pids-limit` cgroup controls during container create/start.

This can happen on nested, rootless, or otherwise constrained Docker hosts. Before this change, operators had to know to set `OPENCLAW_DOCKER_E2E_DISABLE_RESOURCE_LIMITS=1` manually; failed named-container and `--cidfile` attempts could also leave artifacts that blocked the retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Docker run helpers now retry once without OpenClaw-injected default resource caps only when Docker itself reports a daemon/runtime resource-limit create failure. The retry path:

- preserves stderr for the original failure;
- keeps ordinary Docker and container-command failures unchanged;
- caches the runtime resource-cap disable for later runs in the same process;
- cleans failed `--name` / `--cidfile` container artifacts before retrying;
- stops cleanup parsing at Docker's image boundary, so `--name` or `--cidfile` inside the container command cannot trigger cleanup of an unrelated container.

The package fallback helper receives the same behavior because it can run without the shared container helper in package-backed lanes. Explicit user-provided Docker run arguments remain on retry; only OpenClaw's injected default caps are removed.

## User Impact

Developers and CI operators can run Docker E2E lanes on more host configurations without manually disabling resource limits. Normal hosts keep the existing capped Docker runs, and non-resource failures such as missing images or container-command exits still fail immediately without retrying as a different command.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(tavily): fall back to process.env when config SecretRef is unresolvable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tavily_search` and `tavily_extract` fail at runtime with `unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY"` even when `TAVILY_API_KEY` is set in the gateway process environment. The configured `SecretRef` points at an env-backed credential that the active runtime snapshot can't inline-resolve, but the plugin's own call chain already has a `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` fallback — the helper in strict mode throws before that fallback can run. Bundled peers (`brave`, `firecrawl`, `exa`) use `readConfiguredSecretString` from `extensions/web-search-provider-common` and don't hit this; tavily and exa are the only remaining `extensions/*/src/config.ts` helpers still throwing in strict mode.

## Evidence

**Environment:** Linux, Node v24, OpenClaw `v2026.6.8` (commit `8a24f93`), with the patch applied via `prestart.sh` step 7/7 in the contributor's runtime overlay.

**Reproduction (before fix):**

```bash
export TAVILY_API_KEY=***
openclaw config set plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey \
  --ref-provider default --ref-source env --ref-id TAVILY_API_KEY
openclaw infer web search --provider tavily --query ping --limit 1 --json
# → Error: plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey: unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY". Resolve this command against an active gateway runtime snapshot before reading it.
```

**After this patch:** Same command reaches Tavily. With a dummy key, the expected downstream error is `401 Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key` (auth failure, not SecretRef failure). With a live key, the call returns search results.

## Real behavior proof — captured runtime logs (2026-06-21)

Real LLM-driven MCP tool calls captured from the contributor's gateway log
on 2026-06-21, when an agent tried a research query about Tailscale and
the MCP `tavily_search` / `tavily_extract` tools failed for the same
reason. These are the exact log lines:

```
2026-06-21T12:05:16.462+00:00 [tools] tavily_search failed: plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey: unresolved SecretRef "env:default:TAVILY_API_KEY". ## Test coverage
```

helper end-to-end against the bundled SDK (no `vi.mock` — production
resolver path runs against `resolveSecretInputString` with `mode: "inspect"`

- does **NOT** fall back when the configured SecretRef is an `exec` source
- does **NOT** fall back when the configured env SecretRef targets a different env var

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] Integrations (tavily web-search plugin)

## Linked Issue

Fixes a regression where the bundled tavily plugin (added in PR #49200) cannot fall back to `TAVILY_API_KEY` when the configured `plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey` is a SecretRef the active runtime snapshot doesn't inline-resolve. Related closed issues that did not catch this runtime-side gap:

- #76491 — closed as "implemented on current main", but the vendored tavily/exa helpers (`extensions/tavily/src/config.ts`, `extensions/exa/src/config.ts`) still throw in strict mode.
- #82621 — closed by PR #82798 for the CLI `infer web search` path; this PR fixes the runtime plugin path that #82798 left open.

Related: #95112 by @liuhao1024 — closed unmerged (uses the same `mode: "inspect"` core, without the file/exec/non-matching-env allowlist added here). If maintainers prefer that approach, the inspect-mode logic there can be combined with the allowlist gating from this one.

## Approach

Replaces the previous `try/catch` approach with the inspect-mode pattern already used in `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts`:

1. Calls `resolveSecretInputString` with `mode: "inspect"` so unresolved SecretRefs return `configured_unavailable` instead of throwing.
2. Treats `file` and `exec` SecretRefs as `blocked` — never falls through to ambient `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY`.
3. Treats env SecretRefs whose `id` is not `TAVILY_API_KEY` as `blocked` — same reason.
4. Validates the env provider allowlist via `canResolveEnvSecretRefInReadOnlyPath` before reading `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY`.
5. Trims whitespace from the configured id before matching (YAML config may pad env var names).
6. `resolveTavilyApiKey` only falls through to `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` when the configured SecretRef is `missing` (no apiKey configured) — never when it is `blocked`.

This addresses the ClawSweeper review feedback on the previous try/catch revision: the catch-all could silently route Tavily requests through ambient `TAVILY_API_KEY` when the user configured a different explicit SecretRef source (file, exec, or env with a different id), weakening the intended credential boundary.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? **Yes** — behavior change is limited to the previously-broken unresolvable-env-ref case; success path is identical.
- Config/env changes? **No**
- Migration needed? **No**
- CHANGELOG entry: **NOT included** in this PR, per `CONTRIBUTING.md` ("Maintainers or ClawSweeper add the changelog entry when landing user-facing changes"). ClawSweeper's 2026-06-19 review noted the previous manual entry to be removed; this revision drops it.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk:** a stricter upstream caller relies on the resolver throwing so it can surface the error to the user.
  - **Mitigation:** the only caller in this file (`resolveTavilyApiKey`) already has `process.env` and downstream-string fallbacks. The chain in `resolveTavilyApiKey` was always meant to handle an unresolvable ref; the throw was incidental.
- **Risk:** a future plugin re-introduces the same throw pattern.
  - **Mitigation:** the new tests in `extensions/tavily/src/config.test.ts` (3 inspect-mode positive paths, 5 negative paths, 8 cases total) assert the no-throw behavior, so any regression is caught at unit-test time.
- **Risk:** a future user configures a non-`TAVILY_API_KEY` env SecretRef (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY` for tavily) and the ambient `process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY` is silently used.
  - **Mitigation:** the new helper treats such refs as `blocked` and explicitly returns `undefined`; the test suite pins this behavior with dedicated cases.

## Summary

Add explicit `format: "esm"` to `nodeBuildConfig()` in `tsdown.config.ts` for consistency with `nodeWorkspacePackageBuildConfig()` which already has `format: "esm"`.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:**

The root `buildUnifiedDistEntries()` build graph includes bundled plugin public artifacts (e.g. `document-extract/document-extractor.js`) alongside core dist entries. Making the format explicit ensures consistent ESM output across the entire unified build, matching `nodeWorkspacePackageBuildConfig`'s existing explicit ESM format.

**Evidence type:** terminal

**Real environment tested:**

- OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64
- Runtime: Node.js v24.13.0
- Setup: OpenClaw local dev instance, built dist output

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:**

1. Build the project (dist output at `dist/extensions/document-extract/`)
2. Verify the built artifact format:
   ```bash
   grep "export\|module.exports" dist/extensions/document-extract/document-extractor.js
   ```
3. Confirm ESM export syntax, no CJS `module.exports`
4. Verify `nodeBuildConfig` now includes explicit `format: "esm"`
5. Run document extractor unit tests

**Evidence after fix:**

```bash
$ grep "export\|module.exports" dist/extensions/document-extract/document-extractor.js
export { createPdfDocumentExtractor };

$ file dist/extensions/document-extract/document-extractor.js
dist/extensions/document-extract/document-extractor.js: ASCII text
```

The built artifact uses ESM export syntax and dynamic `import("clawpdf")`. No CommonJS `module.exports` or `exports.` patterns are present.

**Observed result after the fix:**

- Build artifact confirmed ESM format: `export { createPdfDocumentExtractor }` (line 82)
- Dynamic `import("clawpdf")` dependency loading at line 6 confirms ESM context
- `nodeBuildConfig` now has explicit `format: "esm"` matching `nodeWorkspacePackageBuildConfig`
- All tests pass: 2/2 document extractor tests

**What was not tested:**

Live end-to-end PDF extraction in a running OpenClaw gateway was not performed. The fix aligns the build configuration at the module format level; the `plugins inspect --json` capability display issue is tracked in PR #91597.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? (`No` / `No`)
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No` / `No`)
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No` / `No`)

**What is the highest-risk area?**

- None — the explicit format is a consistency and defense-in-depth change. tsdown 0.22.1 already defaults to ESM.

**How is that risk mitigated?**

- The explicit `format: "esm"` ensures consistent output regardless of future tsdown default changes.

target.title: ci: gate PR edit automation by changed field
target.body:
Goal: reduce strain on resources by optimizing which PR edits trigger which automations.

## Summary
- gate PR `edited` automation on the fields each workflow actually consumes
- keep ClawSweeper dispatch active for title/body/base edits because it serializes PR title into its activity payload
- skip expensive PR automation for metadata-only edits while preserving title/body/base behavior
- add workflow guard coverage and changed-test routing for the edited-field matrix

## What gets optimized
The optimization is: when a PR is edited, each automation wakes only when that edited field can change the job output.

- `Auto response` (`auto-response`): wakes for title, body, or base edits.
- `ClawSweeper Dispatch` (`dispatch`): wakes for title, body, or base edits.
- `Labeler` (`label`): wakes for title or base edits.
- `Real behavior proof` (`Real behavior proof`): wakes for body or base edits.

Metadata-only edits, such as milestone/assignee/project changes, skip these PR edited-event jobs because none of them read those fields.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #95601.

VoiceOver and keyboard users can open the Control UI chat session picker today, but the history experience was still split across partial slices: unreadable scoped session keys when labels are missing, no direct rename action in the chat picker, and sidebar recent sessions that did not expose separate switch/reopen and rename controls with clear accessible names.

This PR makes both the chat session picker and the sidebar recent-session history expose human-readable titles, timestamps, active-state text, switch/reopen controls, and rename controls through standard keyboard-focusable controls.

## Scope / Overlap Decision

This branch is intentionally a combined Control UI session-history accessibility implementation. It includes the derived-title loading/display scope that overlaps the narrower sidebar/picker title work in #94544, then extends that baseline with switch/reopen semantics, rename controls, sidebar coverage, shared persisted-label handling, and exact-head browser proof.

Maintainers can treat this PR as the candidate canonical fix for #95601 if they prefer one combined picker + sidebar accessibility branch. If maintainers prefer a narrower derived-title-only UX first, #94544 can still be considered separately and this PR can remain paused. This PR does not close or mutate sibling PRs automatically.

## Summary

- requests `includeDerivedTitles` for chat/recent-session loads so unlabeled conversations get readable derived titles instead of raw session keys
- exposes each picker row as a keyboard-reachable switch action with a readable accessible name containing title, timestamp metadata, and active-state text
- adds a keyboard-reachable rename action beside each picker/sidebar row, reusing one shared `promptAndRenameChatSession` helper around `sessions.patch`
- preserves chat-scoped refresh parameters, including `includeDerivedTitles`, after label changes
- updates the sidebar recent-session list so each row exposes separate switch/reopen and rename controls with title, timestamp, and active-state announcements
- keeps the existing New Session control reachable with its existing `aria-label`
- updates generated locale bundles after adding the new English picker/sidebar action strings

## Accessibility Notes

The picker now uses a regular list of session rows rather than an ARIA listbox. Each row contains separate, focusable controls for:

- switching/reopening the session (`Switch to session: <title> · <timestamp> · Active` when current)
- renaming the session (`Rename session: <title> · <timestamp> · Active` when current)

The sidebar recent-session history follows the same pattern: each row is a list item with a link-style switch/reopen control plus a separate rename button. The active session uses `aria-current="page"` and also includes explicit `Active` text in the accessible name.

This avoids mixing ARIA `option` semantics with sibling action buttons while preserving keyboard navigation through standard links/buttons.

## Session Label Write Path

The picker and sidebar both route through `promptAndRenameChatSession`, which is the single UI helper that:

- checks connection/client availability
- prompts with the existing label or fallback display title
- converts blank input to `{ label: null }`
- calls `sessions.patch` with chat-scoped refresh options and `includeDerivedTitles`

This keeps the persisted label behavior centralized even though two UI entry points expose the same rename action.

- Added jsdom coverage that verifies sidebar recent sessions expose New Session, readable title, timestamp, active state, switch/reopen, and rename accessible controls.
- Added jsdom coverage that verifies sidebar recent-session rename uses the shared helper with chat-scoped refresh parameters and derived-title loading preserved.
- Added focused helper coverage for rename, blank-label clearing, cancelled prompt behavior, and shared `sessions.patch` arguments.
- Added controller coverage for forwarding `includeDerivedTitles` and for patch refresh override preservation.

target.title: fix(memory): restore memorySearch provider auto-detection
target.body:
## Summary

After upgrading to 2026.6.1, the `memorySearch` provider silently resets to `"openai"` when no provider is explicitly configured. Previously (2026.5.26) the default was `"auto"`, which correctly auto-selected an available embedding provider (e.g. `gemini-embedding-001` for Google AI Studio users).

The regression was introduced in commit `4d89e00c50` ("feat(embeddings): add OpenAI-compatible core provider (#85269)") which hardcoded the unresolved default to `"openai"` (`DEFAULT_MEMORY_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER`), bypassing the auto-select mechanism.

Fixes #90787

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: memorySearch provider silently defaults to "openai" when not configured, instead of "auto". This breaks vector search for users without an OpenAI API key — the index identity check compares against an empty string and permanently pauses vector search.

**Real setup tested**: Node v24.13.1 running on Linux x86_64, on a local worktree branch of openclaw/openclaw@main (commit bf872b30cd). Verifying the mergeConfig default value fix that restores "auto" as the default memorySearch provider.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/memory-search.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:

Terminal capture of the actual test run:

```
> node scripts/test-projects.mjs "src/agents/memory-search.test.ts"

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  35 passed (35)
   Start at  23:28:38
   Duration  6.22s (transform 2.82s, setup 0ms, import 5.37s, tests 500ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 16.33s
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 35 tests pass. The key behavioral changes verified by the updated test expectations:

- `defaults provider to auto when unspecified` — unconfigured provider now resolves to `"auto"` instead of `"openai"`
- `preserves explicit auto provider config` — explicitly setting `"auto"` is preserved through config resolution
- All existing explicit provider tests remain passing: `"openai"`, `"local"`, `"none"`, and custom provider aliases all resolve identically to pre-fix behavior

**What was not tested**: End-to-end verification with live embedding providers (Google AI Studio, OpenAI) was not performed — that would require live API keys and a running OpenClaw gateway. The fix is validated at the config-resolution unit test level (`memory-search.test.ts`), which is the exact layer where the regression was introduced and where the default provider value is resolved.

## Tests and validation

| Test Type | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Unit Tests | ✅ | 35/35 passed |

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**Yes** — users who did not configure `memorySearch.provider` will now get `"auto"` behavior (auto-select available provider) instead of being forced to `"openai"`. This restores the 2026.5.26 behavior. Users who explicitly configured a provider are unaffected.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**No** — only the unconfigured default value changed; all explicit configurations are preserved identically.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**No** — this is a config-layer default value change only.

What is the highest-risk area?
- Users who explicitly set `provider: "openai"` are unaffected.
- Users who explicitly set `provider: "auto"` are unaffected (the value is now preserved through the config layer instead of being resolved at config time).
- The only behavioral change is for users with no `provider` setting — they regain auto-select functionality.

How is that risk mitigated?
- All existing unit tests pass, including explicit provider configuration tests.
- The change is a one-line default value restoration.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review

target.title: fix(feishu): parse all merge-forward sub-messages and extract interactive card text
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: Feishu merge_forward messages containing interactive/card sub-messages (tables, dashboards, report cards) were silently dropped or rendered as bare `[interactive]`. Two bugs: (1) `parseMergeForwardContent` only included sub-messages with `upper_message_id`, but interactive cards may lack this field; (2) `formatSubMessageContent` had no case for `"interactive"` and fell through to the generic `[contentType]` format.

**Solution**: (1) Broaden the sub-message filter to include all items except the root merge_forward container; (2) Add an `"interactive"` case that reuses `parseInteractiveCardContent` from `send.ts` — the same parser already used in production for fetched message card rendering.

**What changed**: 
- `extensions/feishu/src/bot-content.ts`: +14/-2 — filter fix + interactive card parsing via shared `parseInteractiveCardContent`
- `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts`: +122 — 2 new regression tests (unit + integration with mocked Feishu API)
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: +1/-1 — export `parseInteractiveCardContent`

**What did NOT change**:
- The `parseInteractiveCardContent` parser itself — unchanged, just exported
- Other sub-message type handling (text, image, sticker, etc.) — unchanged
- The Feishu API fetch path for merge_forward detail — unchanged

Fixes #77909

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu merge-forward messages contain sub-messages from multiple users collapsed into a single card. The current parser only extracts the outer message text, missing interactive card content and sub-message text embedded in the merge-forward structure. This causes Feishu users to lose context when forwarded messages contain interactive elements.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: Feishu merge_forward messages containing interactive/card sub-messages were dropped or rendered as bare `[interactive]` placeholder text. Card header titles, table data, and body content were lost before reaching the agent.

**Real setup tested**:
- **Runtime**: Node 24.13, Linux x86_64
- **Branch**: `fix/issue-77909-feishu-merge-forward` rebased onto `upstream/main` (`8c09419f2`)
- **Test runner**: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (project-standard wrapper)
- **Vitest**: 4.1.8

**Root cause — two independent bugs in the same code path**:

Bug 1 (filter): `parseMergeForwardContent` at `bot-content.ts:230` originally used:
```typescript
const subMessages = items.filter((item) => item.upper_message_id);
```
Interactive/card items returned by the Feishu merge_forward detail API may not include `upper_message_id`. These items were filtered out before reaching `formatSubMessageContent`, so their content was completely lost.

Bug 2 (format): `formatSubMessageContent` in `bot-content.ts:198` had no case for `contentType === "interactive"`, falling through to `default: return `[${contentType}]``. Even if interactive items passed the filter, they'd render as `[interactive]` with no extracted text.

**Detailed fix trace** (specific code changes in `bot-content.ts`):

Filter fix (`bot-content.ts:235-238`):
```typescript
const subMessages = items.filter(
  (item) => Boolean(item.upper_message_id) || item.msg_type !== "merge_forward",
);
```
Now includes items with `upper_message_id` (original behavior) OR items that are NOT root merge_forward containers (new: catches interactive cards, images, text without parent ref).

Format fix (`bot-content.ts:201-203`):
```typescript
case "interactive":
  return parseInteractiveCardContent(parsed);
```
Reuses the production-grade parser that handles template variables (`{variable}`), i18n element tags (`{{i18n key}}`), body.elements (div, markdown, lark_md), and post content fallback. This is the same parser used by `getMessageFeishu` for regular fetched messages.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` on the rebased `fix/issue-77909-feishu-merge-forward` branch at Node 24.13 Linux x86_64

**After-fix evidence**:
```
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.8
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  89 passed (89)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 23.79s
```

Two new regression tests added:

1. **Unit test**: "includes interactive sub-messages without upper_message_id (regression #77909)" — directly calls `parseMergeForwardContent` with a card containing header "Weekly Report" and Sales/Cost body elements. Verifies card text is extracted when `upper_message_id` is absent.

2. **Integration test**: "expands merge_forward interactive card sub-messages (regression #77909)" — via `dispatchMessage` with mocked Feishu API returning an interactive card "Q2 Sales Dashboard" with Revenue/Profit data. Verifies `BodyForAgent` contains header title, body text, and accompanying text message.

**Observed result after the fix**: Card content like headers ("Q2 Sales Dashboard"), table data ("Revenue: ¥50,000", "Profit: ¥12,300"), and markdown body text now correctly reach the agent's `BodyForAgent`. The shared `parseInteractiveCardContent` parser ensures consistent rendering between merge_forward interactive cards and directly-fetched interactive messages. Before: `[interactive]` or silently dropped; after: full card text extraction via shared production parser.

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu tenant with real merge_forward messages containing interactive cards. This requires a Feishu app with bot credentials, a group chat with merge_forward messages containing interactive card content, and active WebSocket event delivery. Feishu/Lark tenant access is not available for external contributors — see note below.

**Evidence provenance**: Terminal output from real local checkout of rebased `fix/issue-77909-feishu-merge-forward` on Node 24.13.1 / Linux x86_64, 2026-06-23. The two prior commits (`ea066aeb8` and `74ecd7198`) were squashed into one clean commit, and the CI re-run trigger commit (`e047257a5`) was dropped.


## Evidence

### Vitest

All Feishu message parsing tests pass with zero regressions.

### Test coverage

The new parsing logic correctly extracts sub-messages and interactive card text from all merge-forward variants tested.

## Tests and validation
| Test Type | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| Unit Tests | ✅ 89/89 | bot.test.ts — all passing including 2 new regression tests |
| Rebase | ✅ | Clean rebase onto upstream/main, 1 squashed commit |
| Scope | ✅ | 3 feishu files only, CI trigger commit removed |

## Design decisions

**Why reuse `parseInteractiveCardContent` from `send.ts` instead of a simpler local extractor?**

The first implementation (commit `ea066aeb8`, later superseded) used a local `extractInteractiveText()` that only handled basic header/body text traversal. ClawSweeper review correctly identified this as a maintenance risk — two parsers for the same card format would inevitably drift over time as the Feishu card schema evolves or new features are added to the production parser.

The shared parser in `send.ts` handles a comprehensive set of Feishu interactive card features: template variable substitution (`{variable}` → resolved value), i18n element tags (`{{i18n key}}` → translated text via the i18n registry), body.elements iteration (div with text content, markdown blocks, lark_md inline formatting), post content fallback (cards that embed their text in a post-style content field), and config-level text extraction. All of these are potentially relevant to merge_forward interactive cards, which can contain the same card types as directly-fetched messages.

Exporting the function (`function` → `export function`) is a minimal API surface change — the function signature, behavior, and callers are all unchanged. The only difference is that `bot-content.ts` can now import and call it for merge_forward cards. This is the same pattern used by `bot-content.ts`'s existing import of `saveMessageResourceFeishu` from `media.js` — cross-module imports within the same extension are standard practice.

**Why "include all non-root items" instead of "include items with known msg_types"?**

A whitelist of known types would silently drop any future Feishu message types added to merge_forward payloads. The exclusion-based approach ("everything except the root container") is forward-compatible: new message types automatically pass through to `formatSubMessageContent`, which handles unknown types gracefully via the `[${contentType}]` fallback that renders a readable placeholder rather than dropping content entirely.

The root container is excluded because it's always `msg_type: "merge_forward"` and contains only wrapper metadata (merge_forward header/title), not user-visible sub-message content. Including it would produce a duplicate/nested "Merged and Forwarded Message" label. The exclusion uses `item.msg_type !== "merge_forward"` as a negative check — any item whose msg_type IS merge_forward is the container, and any item whose msg_type is anything else (text, image, interactive, sticker, etc.) is a sub-message worth rendering.

**Why can't this be tested with a live Feishu tenant?**

Feishu open platform requires enterprise/organization certification for app creation. Lark international version is more permissive for individual developers but may require network access that is not available from all environments. The OpenClaw QA credential pool (Convex broker) requires write/maintain repository permissions that external contributors do not have. The fix is validated by unit tests using exact Feishu interactive card JSON fixtures matching the documented card message schema, including header.title with plain_text tags, body.elements with div/markdown/lark_md content, and the standard Feishu message envelope structure.

**Why can't this be tested with a live Feishu tenant?**

Feishu open platform requires enterprise/org certification for app creation (personal developers may face restrictions). Lark international version is more permissive but requires network access that may not be available. The OpenClaw QA credential pool (Convex broker) requires write/maintain repository permissions. External contributors cannot access any of these paths. The fix is validated by unit tests using exact Feishu card JSON fixtures matching the documented interactive card schema.

## Risk checklist

**What is the highest-risk area of this change?**

The broadened sub-message filter could theoretically include unexpected item types from the Feishu API that were previously excluded. If the Feishu API returns items with `msg_type` values not handled by `formatSubMessageContent`, they would render as `[unknown_type]` instead of being silently dropped.

**Risk level**: Low risk — `formatSubMessageContent` has a `default: return `[${contentType}]`` fallback for unknown types, so any unexpected sub-message types from the Feishu API produce visible-but-safe placeholder text rather than crashing the handler or leaking raw JSON data into the agent body. The root container exclusion relies on `msg_type !== "merge_forward"` which is the stable API contract for merge_forward wrapper items — this field has been consistent across Feishu API versions.

**Mitigation**: The two new regression tests cover both the filter path (items without `upper_message_id`) and the format path (interactive card content extraction). The integration test mocks the full Feishu API round-trip: `im.message.get` returning merge_forward detail items, `dispatchMessage` processing through the complete handler chain, and `finalizeInboundContext` producing the final agent body. The unit test directly exercises `parseMergeForwardContent` with the exact card JSON fixture from the issue report. The existing 87 bot tests verify zero regressions in other Feishu message handling paths. The `parseInteractiveCardContent` parser is production-proven — it's the same code path used for every directly-fetched Feishu interactive message.

**Merge risk declaration**:
- `merge-risk: 🚨 message-delivery` — Changes what the agent sees for merge_forward messages. Previously dropped or placeholder content is now rendered as readable text. This is a bug fix restoring correct behavior: the agent should see card content, not `[interactive]`.

## Current review state
**What is the next action?** Maintainer review requested. Code changes are mature (one review cycle completed), all 89 feishu tests pass, and the `triage: needs-real-behavior-proof` gate requires maintainer decision on proof adequacy.

## Summary What problem does this PR solve? Resolves an issue where external plugin channels relying solely on `actions: { handleAction }` (without an explicit `outbound` capability) were incorrectly routed to the `internal-source-reply` sink when using `message(action=send)` without a `to` parameter. Why does this matter now? It prevents valid custom channel plugins (like Lansenger) from silently failing or misrouting messages to the internal sink. What is the intended outcome? Valid custom channels are properly recognized by the fallback routing logic and receive outbound messages natively. What is intentionally out of scope? Changes to official bundled plugins or adding new outbound capabilities; this only touches the fallback validation logic in `internal-source-reply.ts`. What does success look like? `shouldUseInternalSourceReplySink` correctly evaluates plugins lacking an `outbound` object by checking `plugin?.actions?.handleAction` instead of instantly failing when `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` returns `undefined`.
